entities.summary:
Étienne de Bar, sometimes Stephen of Bar, was a French cardinal and nephew of Pope Calixtus II, who played a pivotal role in the politics of the Catholic Church during the 12th century.

Born into a prominent family, de Bar's early life and education would have been heavily influenced by his connection to the papacy.

As a cardinal, de Bar participated in several high-profile events, including the Second Council of Lyons in 1274, where he voted in favor of the union with the Eastern Orthodox Church. This decision had significant consequences for the balance of power within the Church and its relations with the Eastern Empire.

De Bar's legacy extends beyond his participation in this council, as he is remembered for his efforts to promote the Catholic Church's interests in Western Europe during a time of significant cultural and religious upheaval.

The passing of Étienne de Bar in 1164 marked the end of an era in the Church's relations with the papacy, as his nephew Calixtus II would go on to play a crucial role in shaping the Church's policies in the centuries that followed.
